q: Which of the following molecules exhibits optical isomerism due to axial chirality rather than a traditional asymmetric carbon atom?
explain: 1,3-diphenylallene possesses axial chirality without an asymmetric center.

q: For a reaction with the rate law Rate = k[A]²[B], what is the overall reaction order and how does the rate change if [A] is halved and [B] is doubled?
explain: Overall order is 2+1=3. Rate factor = (1/2)² × (2) = 1/2, so the rate halves.

q: What is the hybridization and geometric shape of the tetracyanonickelate(II) ion, [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻?
explain: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand forcing electron pairing in Ni²⁺ (d⁸), resulting in dsp² square planar configuration.

q: Why does the nitro group in nitrobenzene direct incoming electrophiles predominantly to the meta position?
opts: It withdraws electron density inductively and by resonance, destabilizing the carbocation intermediate at ortho and para positions more severely than at the meta position.
It activates the ortho and para positions through hyperconjugation.
It acts as a strong nucleophile that preferentially attacks the meta position.
It sterically hinders the meta position while leaving ortho and para open.
explain: The -NO₂ group is strongly electron-withdrawing (-I and -R), creating positive charges on ortho/para resonance structures that make them unfavorable.

q: For the exothermic reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), how does an increase in temperature affect the equilibrium constant (Kc) and the yield of SO₃?
explain: According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature for an exothermic reaction shifts equilibrium backwards, reducing both Kc and product yield.

q: A solution has a pH of 11.4 at 25°C. What is the hydroxide ion concentration [OH⁻] in mol/dm³?
Which reagent distinguishes between terminal alkynes and internal alkynes?
explain: Terminal alkynes form a white precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO₃.

q: What mass of copper is deposited when a current of 2.5 A flows through CuSO₄ solution for 1 hour 36 minutes 30 seconds? (Cu = 63.5, F = 96500 C/mol)
In the Contact Process, why is SO₃ dissolved in concentrated H₂SO₄ rather than directly in water?
opts: Direct reaction forms a dense acid mist that is difficult to condense
Water decomposes SO₃ into SO₂ and O₂
It forms an explosive mixture with water
explain: SO₃ reacts violently with water to produce an uncontrollable fog of H₂SO₄ droplets.

q: How many structural isomers exist for the molecular formula C₄H₉Br?
explain: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

q: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
explain: PbO reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salts and water.

q: Calculate the solubility product Ksp of PbI₂ if its solubility in pure water at 25°C is 1.3 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³.
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(OH)CH₂COOH?
explain: Carboxylic acid takes priority at C-1, placing the hydroxyl group at C-3.

q: Which transition metal ion is colourless in aqueous solution?
explain: Sc³⁺ has a 3d⁰ configuration with no d-d electronic transitions.

q: A gas occupies 400 cm³ at 27°C and 750 mmHg. What volume will it occupy at s.t.p.? (s.t.p. = 0°C, 760 mmHg)
Which compound undergoes haloform reaction with iodine and aqueous NaOH?
explain: Propan-2-ol oxidizes to propanone, which contains the CH₃CO- group required for the iodoform test.

q: What is the oxidation state of chromium in the dichromate ion, Cr₂O₇²⁻?
In the extraction of aluminium by electrolysis, cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to alumina primarily to?
opts: Lower the melting point and increase conductivity
explain: Cryolite lowers the melting point of Al₂O₃ from ~2050°C to ~950°C.

q: Which intermolecular force accounts for the unusually high boiling point of hydrogen fluoride compared to HCl?
explain: Strong hydrogen bonds form between highly electronegative F and H atoms.

q: How many moles of oxygen are required for the complete combustion of 2 moles of butane (C₄H₁₀)?
explain: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O; 13 moles of O₂ are required.

q: Which salt produces a brown ring when treated with freshly prepared FeSO₄ and concentrated H₂SO₄?
explain: The brown ring test confirms the presence of nitrate ions (NO₃⁻).

q: What happens to the rate of a reaction when a positive catalyst is introduced?
explain: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy.

q: Which polymer is formed by condensation polymerization?
explain: Nylon-6,6 is formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid with the elimination of water.

q: An element X has atomic number 17 and element Y has atomic number 20. What is the formula and bond type of their compound?
explain: Y (Ca) loses 2 electrons to two X (Cl) atoms to form ionic YX₂.

q: When excess ammonia solution is added to aqueous CuSO₄, what is observed?
opts: A light blue precipitate insoluble in excess
explain: Cu(OH)₂ dissolves in excess NH₃ to form the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex ion, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.
